content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation source ledger before answering.

input.summary:
Full ledger built and traced. Sources of authority: the disclosure and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure); input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority, and no-government-support formalities. The "YOU" passage in conversation.md claims the draft is built on "a self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" — that is drafting-agent prose, is not inventor support, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft text, claims, numerals, or figure briefs; no invention matter was drawn from it.

Claims: every limitation of independent claims 1 (apparatus), 11 (installed clamp assembly) and 14 (method), and of dependents 2-10, 12-13 and 15-17, traces to an exact affirmative disclosure passage — semicircular halves with hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three jaw carriages distributed about the closed frame; radial guides; pivoting concave jaw pads that bear "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; outward carriage springs; cam ring "retained in an annular guide," "segmented," "One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half"; "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring"; follower "received in a respective oblique slot"; wedge driven against "a drive face of the cam ring" rotating the coupled ring "through a limited stroke"; oblique slots giving "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" (claim 6's "same inward travel" is traced to that phrase read with "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"); latch first/over-center positions; force-limiting spring stack "between the latch handle and the wedge"; indicator pin moving "relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing" in "a predetermined compression range" and reporting load, not diameter; mounting boss "outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit" that "does not participate in jaw synchronization"; and the install/remove sequences. No means-plus-function language; antecedent basis checked (claim 3's "the pipe" from claim 2; claims 14 and 17's "the annular guide" from the claim 14 preamble). Statutory classes are apparatus, article and method, all disclosure-supported.

Numerals: all 28 ledger entries (10-26, 30-66) appear in the description with one consistent meaning each, each appears on at least one sheet, and every numeral listed in a figure brief is in the ledger. The two families of "drive face" stay distinct: 44/46 (hinge end) and 48/50 (latch end) couple the segments, while 54 is the "ring drive face" the wedge bears on. Segment-to-half assignments are consistent across sheets: FIG-1 makes 12 the upper half and 14 the lower, FIG-3 places 32 in the upper segment and 34 in the lower, 44/48 on the upper (first) segment and 46/50 on the lower (second), the left junction is the hinge end and the right junction the latch end, matching FIG-1's hinge at the left break and latch at the right.

Figure briefs: FIG-1 through FIG-4 depict only source-disclosed parts. Generic outlines (hinge, latch body, boss, housing, spring stack, wedge block, indicator rod, handle, segment end faces, ring drive face) are declared "shown schematically" in the briefs, the claims and description remain shape-neutral, and no brief-only convention leaks into the application text — 07-drawings and 08-detailed-description contain no "by way of example," no "any closed outline," and no optional embodiment added to justify a rendering choice. Functional-surface statements were checked individually and each is compelled by the source rather than added: matching, abutting segment end faces follow from "complementary drive faces … couple the segments"; the common rotational sense of the three oblique slots follows from "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; the ring drive face at the latch end follows from the wedge being carried by the latch, which the disclosure places at the latch end; no taper, angle, depth, runout or proportion is asserted anywhere. No section line is designated in any view, so no designation-matching issue arises. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in the application text; the briefs' "part names are semantic identifiers only" line is confined to the figure briefs.

One minor internal-consistency defect was found and is reported below: the semantic identifier "pad" is used for the mounting boss 66 in FIG-1 and for the jaw pad 26 in FIG-2. Everything else in the ledger is supported and internally consistent; no unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, description, abstract, or figure briefs.

findings.title: Semantic identifier "pad" designates two different numbered parts across the figure briefs
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md (geometry bullet for the mounting boss and numeral placement target for 66) versus figures/FIG-2.md (geometry bullet for the jaw pad and numeral placement target for 26)
findings.detail: Within FIG-1 the word "pad" names the mounting boss 66, while within FIG-2 the same word names the jaw pad 26 and the mounting boss is instead called a "small rectangular projection." Numeral 66 and numeral 26 each keep a single meaning in the description and the numeral ledger, so this is not a source-fidelity defect, but the renderer-facing identifier is not stable across sheets: the same word points at the boss on one sheet and at the concave jaw pad on the next, which can misdirect leader placement for 26 and 66. FIG-2 already uses "projection" for the boss, so aligning FIG-1 to FIG-2 removes the collision with no change of technical content and no change to any application text.
findings.evidence: FIG-1.md: "A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular pad on the outer boundary of the annular frame body at the upper right" and "66: well inside the rectangular pad at the upper right." FIG-2.md: "On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge", "26: well inside the concave edged pad at the lower right", and "66: well inside the small rectangular projection at the upper right."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, replace "A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular pad on the outer boundary of the annular frame body at the upper right" with "A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular projection on the outer boundary of the annular frame body at the upper right", and replace the placement target "66: well inside the rectangular pad at the upper right." with "66: well inside the small rectangular projection at the upper right." Make no other change; the description, claims, ledger, and depicted structures are unaffected.
